costNote: Claims paid and reserved for, plus the cost of adjusting them — an insurer's cost of goods sold. The quarter included $234M of pre-tax catastrophe losses, partly offset by $179M of favorable development on old reserves.

opex.name: Acquisition expenses
opex.note: Commissions and the cost of winning the premiums — mostly broker and agent commissions.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Staff and running the three segments (insurance, reinsurance, mortgage).

opex.name: Corporate, deal & amortization
opex.note: $30M amortization of intangibles, $17M transaction costs and $5M net corporate expenses.

otherDetail.label: Interest expense
otherDetail.note: Cost of debt — up from $37M after Arch's June 2026 capital raise.

otherDetail.label: Income from operating affiliates
otherDetail.note: Arch's share of profits from operating affiliates; Arch reports this line after tax, and it is grouped here so the statement balances.

footerNote: Insurer layout: 'revenue' is net premiums earned plus investment and other income; claims (losses & loss adjustment) are the direct-cost block. Net income is the $1,035M available to Arch; common shareholders received $1,025M after $10M of preferred dividends. Income from operating affiliates ($33M), reported after tax by Arch, is grouped into other income.

oneTimers.label: Catastrophes vs old reserves
oneTimers.text: $234M of pre-tax catastrophe losses hit the quarter, while prior-year reserves developed favorably by $179M — the two largely offset inside the claims line.

segments.name: Premiums earned & underwriting income
segments.note: Net premiums earned of $4,014M (insurance $1,937M, reinsurance $1,807M, mortgage $270M) plus $61M of other underwriting income. Gross written premiums were $5,391M before ceding $1,546M to reinsurers.

segments.name: Investment income, net
segments.note: $451M of net investment income plus $224M from equity-method investments, minus $99M of net realized losses as rising rates hit bond values.

sources.label: Arch Capital Q3 2026 earnings release — SEC EDGAR Ex-99.1 (8-K, Oct 27, 2026)

takeaways.text: Underwriting income of $702M (insurance $108M, reinsurance $393M, mortgage $201M) with a combined ratio excluding catastrophes and prior-year development of 81.2%.
takeaways.title: Underwriting carried the quarter

takeaways.text: EPS of $3.00 was down from $3.56 a year ago: investments swung to $99M of realized losses (vs $210M of gains) as rates rose, even though underwriting improved.
takeaways.title: Profit down on investment marks

takeaways.text: Arch returned $1.4B via buybacks in one quarter — a big reason book value per share slipped 0.2% sequentially to $67.90 despite a profitable quarter.
takeaways.title: Huge buyback quarter

verdict: Textbook Arch: underwriting profit of $702M did the heavy lifting while rising rates nicked the investment portfolio.
